The Federal Government has announced a social media challenge offering university students cash prizes of up to N1.5m for creating videos promoting the protection of the country’s power infrastructure. The challenge, tagged #SecureTheGrid, is being organised by the Federal Ministry of Power in partnership with the National Association of University Students as part of activities marking International Students’ Day. Announcing the initiative on Friday on Instagram, the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said the challenge was designed to encourage students to take an active role in protecting electricity infrastructure. “Power infrastructure belongs to all of us, and YOU can help secure it!” Tegbe said in a message announcing the challenge. How to participate Interested university students are required to create a 45 to 60-second video explaining why power infrastructure should be protected. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources According to the minister, participants must upload their videos on their personal TikTok, Instagram, Facebook or X accounts, with their full names and institutions included in the captions. They are also required to use the hashtags #SecureTheGrid and #ProtectPowerAssets when posting their entries. Participants posting on X, Instagram and TikTok are expected to tag @JosephOTegbe and @fmp_ng, while those using Facebook should tag @fmpnigeria and @nausnational. FG doubles Gombe transmission capacity to 480MW Elektron Energy acquires Daystar Power Group from Shell FG targets 24-hour power supply in Lagos, others Tegbe also urged participants to encourage their friends to like and share their videos, noting that winners would be determined by the number of engagements recorded on each entry. Prizes to be won The challenge offers N1m to the first-place winner, with an additional N500,000 for the winner’s Students’ Union Government, N500,000 for the second-place winner, N200,000 for the third-place winner and N100,000 each for 12 consolation prize winners, with two selected from each of the six geopolitical zones. The school with the highest number of participants will also receive N1m. The minister encouraged students to be creative and use their voices to promote the protection of the national grid. “Be creative. Be bold. Add your voice to protecting the grid,” he said. Entries for the #SecureTheGrid National Social Media Challenge will close on November 30, 2026. Interested students are encouraged to publish their videos before the deadline and ensure they follow the participation guidelines.
